section_headings: What are the genetics of I-95?
Why is the strain called I-95?

article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Balanced hybrid
Genetics: Triangle Kush × (Legend OG × Stardawg IX2)
Breeder: Top Dawg Seeds
THC Content: 20–28%
CBD Content: Usually below 1%
Terpene Profile: Myrcene , limonene , beta-caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Diesel fuel, sour lemon, pine, Skunk
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–10 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: early to mid-October
Indoor Yield: Medium to high under favorable conditions
Outdoor Yield: Moderate to high
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

I-95 is not built around candy, cream, or tropical fruit. Its identity comes from the other side of American cannabis breeding: gasoline, sour chemicals, pine cleaner, wet earth, Skunk, and the penetrating OG aroma that can announce itself before the container is fully opened. The cultivar brings together three celebrated East Coast and Kush-era genetic lines—Triangle Kush, Legend OG, and Stardawg IX2—and became closely associated with Top Dawg Genetics breeder Money Mike and JJ-NYC. Contemporary records from breeders working directly with the genetics consistently preserve the formula as Triangle Kush × (Legend OG × Stardawg IX2).

Its name references Interstate 95, the highway running along much of the eastern United States, and the symbolism fits the pedigree unusually well. Florida’s Triangle Kush occupies one end of the genetic story, while Top Dawg’s Chemdog -heavy Stardawg work represents the Northeast. Rather than smoothing those parents into a generic hybrid, I-95 amplifies their shared fuel character. Dense lime-green flowers, heavy trichomes, sour gas, and a high that can feel mentally alert before becoming physically settled have made the plant a recognizable benchmark for growers who favor old-school Chem and OG marijuana over sweeter modern profiles.
Genetics and Lineage

The original cross is Triangle Kush × (Legend OG × Stardawg IX2). Greenpoint Seeds, which has used I-95 extensively as breeding material, directly credits Money Mike of Top Dawg Genetics with building the strain from those parents. The strain’s historical profile adds more context, describing JJ-NYC and Money Mike as working with a Triangle Kush × Legend OG female and a selected Stardawg IX2 male. This wording explains why some simplified lineage diagrams appear to rearrange the parents while still pointing toward the same core genetic population.

Triangle Kush provides the unmistakable OG foundation. The old Florida cut is associated with lemon, earth, fuel, tight flower structure, and a strong physical effect. Legend OG reinforces the Kush side with deeper gas, pine, earth, and dense resinous flowers. Stardawg IX2 shifts the combination toward Chemdog territory, adding sharper chemical funk, frost, vigor, and the aggressive sour-gas character for which Top Dawg became particularly well known. The finished hybrid therefore represents less of a meeting between unrelated genetic families than a concentrated stack of Chem and OG traits.

That foundation also made I-95 valuable to other breeders. Top Dawg itself has continued working the line through I-95 backcross projects, while outside programs have paired it with Stardawg and numerous other cultivars. Greenpoint describes the original cut as an unusually pungent example of East Coast genetics and has used it directly in later breeding work. Its continued use reflects more than nostalgia: breeders value the plant for transferring fuel, resin, potency, and recognizable OG/Chem character into new hybrids.
Effects and Experience

I-95 can initially feel more cerebral than its heavy Kush ancestry suggests. The onset often develops behind the eyes with a sense of mental pressure, sharper attention, and an increasingly euphoric mood. Creative work, conversation, or music may become more absorbing before any serious physical heaviness develops. The effect is not typically as bright or restless as a tropical sativa; instead, it carries a focused, slightly forceful mental quality that mirrors the cultivar’s sharp aroma.

A calmer physical layer follows. Muscular tension may begin to ease while the mind remains relatively active, creating the balanced character behind its common 50/50 classification. As dosage rises, however, the OG and Chem ancestry becomes more obvious. The body can feel progressively heavier, concentration may soften, and the strain becomes more compatible with an evening at home than demanding activity.

Potency varies substantially. Verified clone material is commonly described around 22–28% THC, while commercial flower has also appeared closer to the high teens or low 20s. Get Seeds Right Here lists the Money Mike cut around 22–28%, whereas Canna Organix has sold I-95 flower at 23.4% THC and 0.51% CBD. Stronger batches can cause dry mouth, dizziness, anxiety, or impaired concentration in consumers who take more than their tolerance supports.
Medical Benefits

The combination of mental engagement and physical relaxation may interest medical marijuana consumers who dislike weed strains that immediately become sedating. At lower amounts, the cultivar can preserve enough clarity for a relatively functional experience while introducing a softer body sensation. Increasing the dose generally brings the heavier qualities forward, which may make the same flower feel very different later in a session.

That flexibility should not be interpreted as evidence of treatment effectiveness. I-95 has not been clinically demonstrated to treat pain, anxiety, insomnia, depression, PTSD, or another medical condition. High-THC weed can also increase anxiety or cognitive impairment in susceptible individuals. Anyone using cannabis for medical purposes should consider the chemistry of the actual tested batch, personal tolerance, medication interactions, and qualified healthcare guidance rather than relying on a strain name.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Fuel is the center of the profile, but describing I-95 simply as “diesel” misses much of its complexity. Leaf Magazine’s examination of the cultivar emphasizes gasoline, Skunk spray, and a pine-cleaner-like sharpness, while Greenpoint describes sour Skunk and diesel as defining characteristics. Lemon rind, damp soil, rubber, herbs, and chemical solvent can appear beneath the larger gasoline note, giving the flower an aroma closer to a garage or workshop than a bakery.

Myrcene, limonene, and beta-caryophyllene frequently appear among the dominant terpenes in commercial versions. Canna Organix identifies those same three as characteristic of its I-95 flower, while other growers have noted similarly gas-forward profiles. Limonene helps explain the sour lemon edge, caryophyllene reinforces pepper and sharp spice, and myrcene contributes earthy depth. Pine-related aromas may also be strengthened by alpha- and beta-pinene when present.

The smoke usually follows a different sequence from the aroma. Sour lemon and fuel can arrive first, followed by earthy OG, pine, pepper, and a dry chemical finish that lingers on the palate. Consumers accustomed to modern fruit-and-candy cannabis may find the flavor unusually aggressive, but that is precisely the reason gas enthusiasts continue to seek the original cut.
Growing Information

I-95 is generally considered an intermediate cultivar rather than a beginner plant. Verified clone descriptions place indoor flowering around eight to nine weeks, although growers maintaining the Money Mike cut sometimes allow closer to ten weeks depending on phenotype and desired maturity. Get Seeds Right Here lists eight to nine weeks for authenticated clone material, while independent holders of the same cut commonly report roughly 60–70 days.

Growth tends to combine OG architecture with stronger Stardawg vigor. Plants can produce solid lateral branches and dense flowering sites, but canopy management is useful because individual shoots may stretch unevenly after the transition to bloom. Topping and gentle training help expose more of the plant to direct light, while later branch support can become valuable as the resinous flowers gain weight.

No reliable original Top Dawg grams-per-square-meter or outdoor-per-plant yield specification is widely preserved, so precise production numbers should be treated cautiously. Contemporary sources generally place yield in the medium-to-high range rather than describing I-95 as either a low producer or a dedicated commercial biomass plant. Dense flowers require adequate airflow and controlled humidity near maturity. Outdoors, the eight-to-ten-week flowering requirement typically puts harvest around early to mid-October in compatible climates, though actual flower development should determine the final date.
FAQ
What are the genetics of I-95?

I-95 is Triangle Kush × (Legend OG × Stardawg IX2). The cultivar was developed through Top Dawg Genetics and is closely credited to Money Mike, with JJ-NYC also associated with the original breeding work.
Why is the strain called I-95?

The name refers to Interstate 95, the major highway running along the East Coast of the United States. The reference fits a cultivar built from genetic lines strongly associated with Florida, New York, and the wider East Coast cannabis scene.
Is I-95 indica or sativa?

It is best described as a balanced hybrid. The onset often feels mentally focused and euphoric, while stronger physical relaxation develops afterward. The precise indica/sativa percentage is less useful than that two-stage effect profile.
How strong is I-95?

Authentic clone material is commonly associated with approximately 22–28% THC, although commercial flower can test lower or higher. One documented Canna Organix batch contained 23.4% THC and 0.51% CBD.
What does I-95 taste like?
Expect diesel fuel, sour lemon, pine, Skunk, earth, pepper, rubber, and a sharp chemical finish. It is a classic gas-forward marijuana cultivar rather than a sweet dessert strain.
Final Thoughts on I-95

I-95 captures an era of American cannabis breeding when Chem and OG genetics defined premium flower more strongly than candy terpenes or purple coloration. Triangle Kush provides the Florida OG backbone, Legend OG deepens the Kush character, and Stardawg IX2 supplies Chemdog resin and chemical funk. Money Mike and the Top Dawg circle turned those ingredients into a cultivar that smells unmistakably like sour fuel and pine cleaner while retaining a surprisingly balanced mental-and-physical high.

Its long-term importance is visible in breeding catalogs as much as dispensary menus. I-95 has been backcrossed, crossed again to Stardawg, and used as a gas-heavy parent in newer projects because it passes along a profile that is increasingly distinctive in a sweet-dominated market. For cannabis enthusiasts interested in classic American fuel genetics, I-95 remains a useful reference point: dense, frosty, chemically pungent weed with authentic Triangle Kush, Legend OG, and Stardawg ancestry rather than a terpene profile engineered around dessert flavors.
